assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme behind biological nitrogen fixation. Atomic structures of the MoFe protein and FeMo-cofactor, with the interstitial carbide and the ATP-coupled electron transfer, give a chemically concrete mechanism for one of the hardest redox transformations in nature. It fits my view that biological energy conversion should be explained by physical mechanism, with long-range electron and proton delivery gating the chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the structural work and the cofactor architecture. Einsle contributed the high-resolution structure and the carbide assignment. Seefeldt contributed kinetic and spectroscopic mechanism. Dean and Ribbe also contributed substantially, so a three-person limit forces a contestable choice.
assessment.maturity: The structures have been confirmed independently over decades and the central picture is stable. Recent cryo-EM and turnover-state structures are refining the mechanism, so recognition is timely though the substrate-binding mechanism remains partly open.
uncertainties: Which cofactor sites bind N2 and how the E4 state forms is still debated.
Credit among Rees, Dean, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe is not cleanly separable.
From memory I believe Burgess and Hoffman also made major contributions, but they are not in the credited names, so I cannot propose them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to a ubiquitin ligase, either through bifunctional PROTACs or through molecular glues that reprogram cereblon, opened a new pharmacological modality. The work is conceptually original and has produced clinical candidates. It rests on well-defined chemistry of ternary complexes.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed PROTACs. Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains the glue mechanism. Ciulli, Gray and others made strong later contributions, so a three-person limit leaves out important people.
assessment.maturity: Preclinical validation is extensive and clinical trials of degraders are advanced, but no PROTAC drug is approved yet. Some committee members may see this as slightly early.
uncertainties: Clinical proof of benefit is still pending.
The split between PROTAC and glue contributions, and between Crews and Deshaies, could draw dispute.
Whether recognition belongs to chemistry or to medicine is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is the physical principle behind much of respiration, photosynthesis and water oxidation. It is close to my own work on proton transfer in cytochrome c oxidase. Theory and molecular electrocatalysis together explain concerted proton and electron movement, with lasting influence in chemistry and bioenergetics.
assessment.attribution: Hammes-Schiffer supplied the theoretical framework. Mayer and Nocera supplied the key experimental and mechanistic demonstrations. Meyer contributed early, but the three-person configuration is defensible, though the boundaries are somewhat diffuse.
assessment.maturity: The concept is well established and broadly confirmed, but it is spread across many systems. A single sharp discovery is hard to name, which weakens clarity of recognition.
uncertainties: The discovery is diffuse and the prize motivation could be hard to word.
Credit among Meyer, Mayer, Nocera and Hammes-Schiffer is unresolved.
I may overweight this because of my own field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another without double-strand cleavage, by engineering deaminases on a Cas scaffold. The idea is original and clearly chemistry-driven, and it is already used clinically and widely in research. The impact on genome editing is large.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the concept and the work. Komor made the cytosine base editor and Gaudelli the adenine base editor, as first authors. Liu alone could also be defended, but the two lead developers are credited in the candidate.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use and independent replication are strong and the technology has existed since 2016 to 2017. Recognition would be timely. Genome editing was recognized in 2020, which may make the committee cautious about repeating a closely related area.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize could count against it.
Whether first authors should be credited next to Liu is a judgment call.
Long-term safety of editors in patients is still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled siRNA and mRNA medicines, including the COVID-19 vaccines. The chemistry of pKa-tuned lipids and the physical chemistry of lipid self-assembly and membrane fusion are central. The societal impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues developed the lipid nanoparticle formulation process and the ionizable lipid approach. Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan also contributed substantially, so who counts as decisive is a hard question.
assessment.maturity: Clinical and global confirmation is overwhelming. Because the 2023 Medicine prize went to nucleoside modification, a chemistry prize for delivery would be timely and complementary.
uncertainties: Credit between academic and industrial groups is contested and may involve patent disputes.
Specific lipid contributions are hard to trace to individuals.
I am relying on recall rather than verified facts about who invented which lipid.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experiments on electron tunneling through proteins showed how distance and the intervening medium control rates, giving a quantitative basis for biological electron transfer. It underpins respiratory and photosynthetic chain function and complements Marcus theory. It is close to my own field.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear, tightly coupled pair, supported by ruthenium-modified protein experiments. The pairing is clean.
assessment.maturity: The results have been confirmed over decades and are textbook material. Because the work is old, recognition is no longer early and may be seen as belated or lower in priority.
uncertainties: The committee might see it as already covered by Marcus (1992).
The concept of multistep hopping versus single-step tunneling is still being refined.
Gray's age and other contributions may influence the decision.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached very high solar cell efficiencies in a few years and have changed photovoltaic research. The discovery is clear and the impact large, though the chemistry underlying defect tolerance is still being explored.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells. Snaith and Grätzel with Park drove the efficiency and stability advances. Park and Seok also have strong claims, so the attribution is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are replicated, but long-term stability and commercialization remain open. Recognition could be premature on those grounds.
uncertainties: Operational stability and lead toxicity remain unsolved.
Allocation among six credited people is unresolved.
Whether the contribution is a materials discovery or an incremental device advance is arguable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers provides room-temperature, damage-free structures and time-resolved views of reactions in proteins. It matches my interest in combining time-resolved methods with structure to see dynamics in 3D, and it has produced mechanistic insight into photosystems and light-driven proteins.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the method and the first demonstrations. Fromme contributed the photosystem I crystal samples and the initial experiments. Schlichting contributed to time-resolved applications. Hajdu's earlier role in the concept is also significant.
assessment.maturity: The method is well confirmed at several facilities. Its mechanistic payoff is still maturing, so the timing is somewhat early compared with other candidates.
uncertainties: Impact on mainstream structural biology is smaller than that of cryo-EM.
Credit among the founders and the facility builders is unresolved.
Limited access to XFEL beamtime restricts the breadth of use.
